feedback.worked_solution:
On the left side of the graph, we see that as the values of $x$ decrease and approach $-\infty ,$ the graph of the function $g(x)$ moves closer and closer to the horizontal asymptote $y=3.$

Consequently, $g(x)$ approaches the value $3$ as $x$ approaches $-\infty ,$ and we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }g(x)=3.
$$

On the right side of the graph, as the values of $x$ increase and approach $\infty ,$ the graph of the function decrease without bound to $-\infty .$   Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }g(x)=-\infty .
$$
